problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must plan a circuit for a freight truck that will stop at 10 distribution centers:

Center Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (76,29)  
Center Beta: Positioned at grid reference (196,161)  
Center Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (77,139)  
Center Delta: Positioned at grid reference (155,39)  
Center Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (108,180)  
Center Zeta: Positioned at grid reference (192,120)  
Center Eta: Positioned at grid reference (23,173)  
Center Theta: Positioned at grid reference (127,194)  
Center Iota: Positioned at grid reference (59,139)  
Center Kappa: Positioned at grid reference (195,103)

Travel segments between centers are quantified in kilometers with the following precise lengths:
Alpha to Gamma: 110.0 km  
Alpha to Delta: 79.6 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 154.4 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 147.4 km  
Alpha to Eta: 153.4 km  
Alpha to Theta: 172.7 km  
Alpha to Iota: 111.3 km  
Alpha to Kappa: 140.1 km  
Beta to Gamma: 121.0 km  
Beta to Delta: 128.7 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 90.0 km  
Beta to Zeta: 41.2 km  
Beta to Eta: 173.4 km  
Beta to Theta: 76.5 km  
Beta to Iota: 138.8 km  
Beta to Kappa: 58.0 km  
Gamma to Delta: 126.8 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 51.4 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 116.6 km  
Gamma to Eta: 63.8 km  
Gamma to Theta: 74.3 km  
Gamma to Iota: 18.0 km  
Gamma to Kappa: 123.4 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 148.6 km  
Delta to Zeta: 89.1 km  
Delta to Eta: 188.1 km  
Delta to Theta: 157.5 km  
Delta to Iota: 138.6 km  
Delta to Kappa: 75.5 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 103.2 km  
Epsilon to Eta: 85.3 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 23.6 km  
Epsilon to Iota: 63.9 km  
Epsilon to Kappa: 116.2 km  
Zeta to Eta: 177.1 km  
Zeta to Theta: 98.5 km  
Zeta to Iota: 134.4 km  
Zeta to Kappa: 17.3 km  
Eta to Theta: 106.1 km  
Eta to Iota: 49.5 km  
Eta to Kappa: 185.7 km  
Theta to Iota: 87.5 km  
Theta to Kappa: 113.6 km  
Iota to Kappa: 140.7 km

Due to infrastructure limitations, no direct route exists between Center Alpha and Center Beta. Furthermore, a routing mandate stipulates that the final circuit must incorporate exactly one of the following two critical links: either the segment connecting Beta and Gamma, or the segment connecting Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed loop that visits every distribution center precisely once before returning to the initial point of departure.
